# Nubank — 2023 Financial Results & Strategic Overview

## Company Profile

Nubank is a Brazilian fintech company specializing in digital banking, founded on 6 May 2013 and headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil. It was co-founded by **David Vélez** (CEO), **Cristina Junqueira**, and **Edward Wible**. The company operates across the financial services, fintech, and banking industries.

---

## 2023 Financial Results

Nubank posted its **first full-year net profit of approximately US$1 billion** in 2023, a landmark achievement for the digital lender. Key highlights:

- **Full-year net income:** ~US$1 billion (reported in February 2024 as the company's first annual profit at that scale).
- **Customer base:** Surpassed **100 million customers** across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia during 2024, having grown rapidly through 2023. In Brazil alone, Nubank served over 92 million customers by the end of that period.
- **Credit portfolio growth:** The company saw strong year-on-year expansion in its lending book, driven primarily by its Brazilian operations and growing credit portfolios in Mexico.
- **Revenue growth:** Revenue continued to scale significantly, supported by net interest income growth and increasing product adoption per customer.

---

## Customer Growth Trajectory

Nubank's customer growth has been one of the most striking in global fintech:

| Period | Customers |
|---|---|
| Mid-2024 | 100 million milestone |
| Q3 2025 | ~127 million |
| Q2 2026 | ~139 million |

In Brazil, Nubank became the **largest private financial institution by number of customers**, reaching over 62% of the adult population (113 million). It also serves 18.4 million customers in Mexico and over 1 million in Colombia.

---

## Strategic Priorities

Nubank's strategic priorities have centered on several key pillars:

1. **Deepening engagement in Brazil** — With an 86% monthly active rate, Nubank focuses on expanding its product suite (credit, insurance, investments, e-commerce) and evolving into a "super app" for daily financial life.

2. **International expansion** — Beyond its core Latin American markets (Brazil, Mexico, Colombia), Nubank applied for a **US national bank charter** in September 2025 and received conditional OCC approval. The US operations are led by co-founder Cristina Junqueira, with former Central Bank of Brazil president Roberto Campos Neto chairing the US board. The company aims to fully capitalise its US entity within 12 months and launch within 18 months.

3. **AI and technology investment** — Nubank acquired AI firm **Hyperplane** in June 2024 to accelerate AI-first strategies in risk assessment, predictive financial management, and personalized customer advice.

4. **Financial inclusion** — The company has helped 28.4 million Brazilians access their first credit card and has saved customers a cumulative US$28.1 billion in fees.

5. **Pursuing a full banking licence in Brazil** — Nubank announced plans to apply for a banking licence in Brazil in 2026, alongside a planned investment of R$45 billion (~US$8.2 billion) in the Brazilian economy for 2026.

---

## Recent Performance Context (2025–2026)

For additional context on the company's trajectory since 2023:

- **Full-year 2025 revenue:** US$16.3 billion, with all-time high net income of US$895 million per quarter and a 33% return on equity.
- **Q3 2025:** Net income of US$783 million (+39% YoY), revenue of US$4.2 billion (+39%), and a record 31% annualized ROE.
- **Q2 2026:** Quarterly net profit surpassed **US$1 billion** for the first time ($1.06 billion, +49% YoY FX-neutral), with revenue of US$5.88 billion (+39%) and a credit portfolio of US$39.4 billion.

Nubank has been named the **best bank in Brazil by Forbes** and ranked #1 globally among neobanks for eight consecutive years.

Nubank says it has now entered the "bank organisation phase", which it explains involves "satisfying specific OCC conditions alongside pending required approvals from the FDIC and the Federal Reserve". The company states it will focus on "fully capitalising the institution within 12 months and opening the bank within 18 months". 

The US operations will be led by Nubank's co-founder Cristina Junqueira, with Roberto Campos Neto, former president of the Central Bank of Brazil, serving as chairman of the board of directors. [...] Related:

This development follows 

Nubank's authorisation in April 2025 by the Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV)
 to organise as a banking institution in Mexico. In Brazil, where Nubank serves over 110 million customers, the company has announced plans to pursue a full banking licence in 2026.

{"content":"## Nubank (Nu Holdings) — 2023 Full-Year Results Overview

### Customer Growth

Nubank experienced rapid customer expansion throughout 2023. The company pre-announced reaching **79.1 million customers** in Q1 2023 and continued adding users at pace across its three markets — Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. By mid-2023, Nubank had surpassed **80 million Brazilian consumers**, and by the end of the year the total customer base across all markets was approaching the 100-million milestone (which was officially reached in May 2024). In Brazil alone, Nubank served more than **92 million customers** by the time it crossed 100 million total, while Mexico surpassed **7 million** and Colombia exceeded **1 million** users. Nubank became the **first digital banking platform outside of Asia** to achieve this scale.

Additionally, Nubank helped **28.4 million Brazilian customers** gain access to their first credit card, underscoring its role in financial inclusion.

### Revenue & Financial Performance

Nubank's full-year 2023 results showed strong financial momentum:

- **Total revenue** grew significantly year-over-year, driven by expanding credit portfolios and rising net interest income.
- The company posted an **all-time high net income** for the period, with profitability improving markedly. By the full-year 2025 reporting cycle, Nu Holdings reported a record net income of **US$895 million** with a **33% return on equity** — building on the trajectory established in 2023.
- In Q1 2023, Nubank reported strong capitalization with an **18.7% Basel Index** in Brazil and an impressive **efficiency ratio of 39%**, placing it among the most efficient and well-capitalized financial institutions in Latin America.
- Credit quality remained solid, with delinquency rates staying within management expectations.

### Strategic Goals & Priorities

Nubank's strategic priorities during and following 2023 centered on several key themes:

1. **Geographic expansion in Latin America**: Core focus remained on deepening penetration in **Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia**. In Mexico, the launch of a credit card proved a hit, attracting over one million users within the first month. In Colombia, Nubank planned to introduce a digital account in 2023, its fastest-growing market at the time.

2. **Financial inclusion**: CEO David Vélez emphasized removing barriers that kept millions outside the formal financial system, driving real competition and expanding access to services previously reserved for a few.

3. **Super app strategy**: Nubank integrated e-commerce and lifestyle services directly into its banking app, evolving from a transactional tool into a daily utility — a super app approach gaining traction in Latin America.

4. **Operating leverage and efficiency**: CFO Guilherme Lago highlighted that profitability was driven by continuous scale gains in Brazil and improved asset-liability management in Mexico, combining operating leverage with disciplined cost management.

5. **U.S. market entry**: Following the strong 2023–2024 growth trajectory, Nubank announced plans to enter the United States in September 2025, applying for a U.S. bank charter with former Brazilian central bank chief Roberto Campos Neto chairing the board of its U.S. business.

6. **Investment in Brazil**: Nubank committed to significant investment in Brazilian infrastructure, with approximately **US$50 billion** allocated to expanding offices and networks across the country, supporting sustained and responsible portfolio growth at scale.

7. **Customer-centricity and engagement**: Nubank achieved a monthly engagement rate of **86%** and was named the **best bank in Brazil and Mexico** by Forbes, while the Central Bank of Brazil recognized it as having one of the lowest complaint rates in the sector.

## Nubank (Nu Holdings) — 2023 Full-Year Results Overview

### Customer Growth

Nubank experienced rapid customer expansion throughout 2023. The company pre-announced reaching **79.1 million customers** in Q1 2023 and continued adding users at pace across its three markets — Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. By mid-2023, Nubank had surpassed **80 million Brazilian consumers**, and by the end of the year the total customer base across all markets was approaching the 100-million milestone (which was officially reached in May 2024). In Brazil alone, Nubank served more than **92 million customers** by the time it crossed 100 million total, while Mexico surpassed **7 million** and Colombia exceeded **1 million** users. Nubank became the **first digital banking platform outside of Asia** to achieve this scale.

Additionally, Nubank helped **28.4 million Brazilian customers** gain access to their first credit card, underscoring its role in financial inclusion.

### Revenue & Financial Performance

Nubank's full-year 2023 results showed strong financial momentum:

- **Total revenue** grew significantly year-over-year, driven by expanding credit portfolios and rising net interest income.
- The company posted an **all-time high net income** for the period, with profitability improving markedly. By the full-year 2025 reporting cycle, Nu Holdings reported a record net income of **US$895 million** with a **33% return on equity** — building on the trajectory established in 2023.
- In Q1 2023, Nubank reported strong capitalization with an **18.7% Basel Index** in Brazil and an impressive **efficiency ratio of 39%**, placing it among the most efficient and well-capitalized financial institutions in Latin America.
- Credit quality remained solid, with delinquency rates staying within management expectations.

### Strategic Goals & Priorities

Nubank's strategic priorities during and following 2023 centered on several key themes:

1. **Geographic expansion in Latin America**: Core focus remained on deepening penetration in **Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia**. In Mexico, the launch of a credit card proved a hit, attracting over one million users within the first month. In Colombia, Nubank planned to introduce a digital account in 2023, its fastest-growing market at the time.

2. **Financial inclusion**: CEO David Vélez emphasized removing barriers that kept millions outside the formal financial system, driving real competition and expanding access to services previously reserved for a few.

3. **Super app strategy**: Nubank integrated e-commerce and lifestyle services directly into its banking app, evolving from a transactional tool into a daily utility — a super app approach gaining traction in Latin America.

4. **Operating leverage and efficiency**: CFO Guilherme Lago highlighted that profitability was driven by continuous scale gains in Brazil and improved asset-liability management in Mexico, combining operating leverage with disciplined cost management.

5. **U.S. market entry**: Following the strong 2023–2024 growth trajectory, Nubank announced plans to enter the United States in September 2025, applying for a U.S. bank charter with former Brazilian central bank chief Roberto Campos Neto chairing the board of its U.S. business.

6. **Investment in Brazil**: Nubank committed to significant investment in Brazilian infrastructure, with approximately **US$50 billion** allocated to expanding offices and networks across the country, supporting sustained and responsible portfolio growth at scale.

7. **Customer-centricity and engagement**: Nubank achieved a monthly engagement rate of **86%** and was named the **best bank in Brazil and Mexico** by Forbes, while the Central Bank of Brazil recognized it as having one of the lowest complaint rates in the sector.

The bank reports that customers have saved a total of US$28.1bn in fees, and has earned it recognition as it was once again named the best bank in Brazil by Forbes, based on a customer survey.

The Central Bank of Brazil has also recognised the bank as one with the lowest rate of complaints in the sector.

## Behind the bank’s growth strategy

After a strong year, closing with a total revenue of US$16.3bn in 2025, Nubank has determined its position as what it terms as the “benchmark for engagement” in Brazil’s financial sector.

Its monthly record rate is 86%, which, paired with a total deposit number of US$41.9bn the results speak for themselves – Nubank is a market leader in Brazil.

The next logical step for the bank is of course to apply for a banking licence. [...] ## What benefit does Nubank currently bring to the Brazilian economy?

Nubank, recently announced as the top fastest-growing neobank, has aided 28.4 million Brazilian customers to gain access to their first credit card.

The bank, self proclaimed as “hungry” to change the status quo, has also supported 18.4 million customers in Mexico and a further one million in Colombia.

David Vélez, Nubank’s CEO and Founder, says: “By removing the barriers that, for decades, kept millions of people outside the formal system, Nubank has driven real competition that expands access to services that used to be reserved for a few.

“Behind every dollar invested, there is a person who now has more money in their pocket, more free time and a better quality of life.” [...] Additionally, the bank aims to launch products and services with customers in mind, specifically regarding financial ease.

Of the investment, ~US$50bn will be allocated to infrastructure for Nubank’s expansion of its offices and network across the country.

Lastly, the company note that the investment supports the strengthening of sustained and responsible growth of the portfolio at scale – encompassing both equity and lending capacity.

Nubank is continuing its upward investment trajectory in Latin America, following the 2026 announcement.

The company's focus remains on Brazil, while also expanding its footprint in key markets.

"The combination of these two things, the operating leverage in Brazil, and the ‍asset liability management in Mexico, led to a large boost to Nubank's consolidated results," Lago said.

The firm's annualized return on equity (ROE), a gauge of profitability, stood at a record ​31%, up from 30% in the same quarter last year. [...] Nubank reached 127 million clients across its operations in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia and in ⁠September announced plans to enter the United States. N26, a German fintech and mobile banking company founded in 2013, offers a comprehensive range of products and account features across both personal and business banking segments:

## Personal Account Tiers

**N26 Standard (Free)**
- Virtual Debit Mastercard with no maintenance fees or minimum balance
- Mobile payments via Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Wallet, and Garmin Pay
- Insights spending tracker
- SEPA Instant Credit transfers

**N26 Smart (€4.90/month)**
- Physical Mastercard debit card (choice of 5 colors)
- Up to 6 virtual cards
- 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals per month
- Up to 10 Spaces sub-accounts with IBANs
- Shared Spaces feature
- Instant Savings account
- Rules for automatic saving

**N26 Go (€9.90/month)**
- All Smart features plus:
- Travel insurance by Allianz Assistance (travel/baggage delays, baggage loss, medical emergencies abroad up to €1,000,000/trip, trip cancellation up to €10,000)
- No foreign transaction fees
- Free foreign-currency ATM withdrawals worldwide
- 3 free stock/ETF trades per month

**N26 Metal (€16.90/month)**
- All Go features plus:
- Stainless-steel metal Mastercard (charcoal black, rose quartz, or slate grey)
- Extended insurance (smartphone theft/damage cover up to €2,000, purchase protection)
- 10 free stock/ETF trades per month
- Priority customer support
- One free airport lounge pass per year
- Market-leading Instant Savings interest rate
- Discounted crypto trading fees

## Business Accounts

N26 offers four business account tiers for freelancers and the self-employed:
- **Business Standard** (Free)
- **Business Smart** (Paid tier with enhanced features)
- **Business Go** (includes travel insurance by Allianz and 0.1% cashback on all Mastercard purchases)
- **Business Metal** (Premium business account)

## Key Product Features

**Spaces Sub-Accounts**
Launched in August 2018, Spaces allows customers to create up to 10 sub-accounts alongside their main account for budgeting and saving goals, each with its own IBAN (introduced in March 2022).

**Investment Products**
- **Stocks, ETFs & ETCs Trading**: Launched in January 2024, customers can buy and sell stocks, ETFs, and ETCs directly in the N26 app at €0.90 per trade (with free trades included on Go and Metal plans)

**N26 Crypto**
Launched initially in Austria in late 2022 and expanded to Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, France, and Spain:
- Access to over 350 cryptocurrencies (one of the largest selections in a European banking app)
- Fully integrated into the N26 app's "Trading" section
- Instant transactions with transparent fee structure
- N26 Metal customers: 1% fee for Bitcoin, 2% for other cryptocurrencies
- Other customers: 1.5% fee for Bitcoin, 2.5% for other cryptocurrencies
- Partnership with Bitpanda Asset Management GmbH for execution and custody

**Insurance Coverage**
Travel and personal insurance packages by Allianz Assistance on Go and Metal tiers, covering:
- Travel delays (up to €500)
- Trip cancellation/interruption (up to €10,000)

{"content":"## N26 — Products and Account Features

**N26** is a German fintech and mobile banking company headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013. It operates across the banking, fintech, and financial/insurance industries. Below is an overview of its main account tiers and features.

---

### Personal Account Plans

| Plan | Monthly Cost | Highlights |
|------|-------------|------------|
| **N26 Standard** | Free | Virtual Debit Mastercard, no maintenance fees, no minimum balance. Mobile payments via Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Wallet, and Garmin Pay. Insights spending tracker. SEPA Instant Credit transfers. |
| **N26 Smart** | €4.90/month | Physical Mastercard debit card (choice of 5 colors), up to 6 virtual cards, 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals/month, up to 10 Spaces sub-accounts (with IBANs), Shared Spaces, Instant Savings account, Rules for automatic saving. |
| **N26 Go** | €9.90/month | Everything in Smart, plus travel insurance by Allianz Assistance (travel/baggage delays, baggage loss, medical emergencies abroad up to €1,000,000/trip, trip cancellation up to €10,000), no foreign transaction fees, free foreign-currency ATM withdrawals worldwide, 3 free stock/ETF trades per month. |
| **N26 Metal** | €16.90/month | Everything in Go, plus stainless-steel metal Mastercard (charcoal black, rose quartz, or slate grey), extended insurance (smartphone theft/damage cover up to €2,000, purchase protection), 10 free stock/ETF trades per month, priority customer support, one free airport lounge pass per year, market-leading Instant Savings interest rate, discounted crypto trading fees. |

---

### Business Account Plans

N26 also offers accounts for freelancers and the self-employed:

- **Business Standard** — Free, with core banking features.
- **Business Smart** — Paid tier with enhanced features.
- **Business Go** — Includes travel insurance by Allianz, 0.1% cashback on all Mastercard purchases.
- **Business Metal** — Premium business account with the highest level of benefits.

---

### Key Features Across Accounts

- **Spaces** — Sub-accounts alongside the main account for budgeting and saving goals (up to 10 on paid plans), each with its own IBAN.
- **Instant Savings** — Flexible savings account accessible anytime.
- **Investments** — Buy and sell stocks, ETFs, and ETCs directly in the N26 app at €0.90 per trade (free trades included with Go and Metal plans).
- **Insurance** — Travel and personal insurance packages by Allianz Assistance on Go and Metal tiers, covering travel delays (up to €500), trip cancellation/interruption (up to €10,000), baggage loss (up to €2,000), medical emergencies abroad (up to €1,000,000), and personal liability (up to €500,000).
- **Deposit Protection** — Funds protected up to €100,000 by the German Deposit Guarantee Scheme.
- **100% Mobile** — Full account management via the N26 app or web app; account opening in minutes with identity verification.
- **Round-ups & Rules** — Automated saving tools to set money aside.
- **Real-time Notifications** — Instant spending alerts for every transaction.

## N26 — Products and Account Features

**N26** is a German fintech and mobile banking company headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013. It operates across the banking, fintech, and financial/insurance industries. Below is an overview of its main account tiers and features.

---

### Personal Account Plans

| Plan | Monthly Cost | Highlights |
|------|-------------|------------|
| **N26 Standard** | Free | Virtual Debit Mastercard, no maintenance fees, no minimum balance. Mobile payments via Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Wallet, and Garmin Pay. Insights spending tracker. SEPA Instant Credit transfers. |
| **N26 Smart** | €4.90/month | Physical Mastercard debit card (choice of 5 colors), up to 6 virtual cards, 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals/month, up to 10 Spaces sub-accounts (with IBANs), Shared Spaces, Instant Savings account, Rules for automatic saving. |
| **N26 Go** | €9.90/month | Everything in Smart, plus travel insurance by Allianz Assistance (travel/baggage delays, baggage loss, medical emergencies abroad up to €1,000,000/trip, trip cancellation up to €10,000), no foreign transaction fees, free foreign-currency ATM withdrawals worldwide, 3 free stock/ETF trades per month. |
| **N26 Metal** | €16.90/month | Everything in Go, plus stainless-steel metal Mastercard (charcoal black, rose quartz, or slate grey), extended insurance (smartphone theft/damage cover up to €2,000, purchase protection), 10 free stock/ETF trades per month, priority customer support, one free airport lounge pass per year, market-leading Instant Savings interest rate, discounted crypto trading fees. |

---

### Business Account Plans

N26 also offers accounts for freelancers and the self-employed:

- **Business Standard** — Free, with core banking features.
- **Business Smart** — Paid tier with enhanced features.
- **Business Go** — Includes travel insurance by Allianz, 0.1% cashback on all Mastercard purchases.
- **Business Metal** — Premium business account with the highest level of benefits.

---

### Key Features Across Accounts

- **Spaces** — Sub-accounts alongside the main account for budgeting and saving goals (up to 10 on paid plans), each with its own IBAN.
- **Instant Savings** — Flexible savings account accessible anytime.
- **Investments** — Buy and sell stocks, ETFs, and ETCs directly in the N26 app at €0.90 per trade (free trades included with Go and Metal plans).
- **Insurance** — Travel and personal insurance packages by Allianz Assistance on Go and Metal tiers, covering travel delays (up to €500), trip cancellation/interruption (up to €10,000), baggage loss (up to €2,000), medical emergencies abroad (up to €1,000,000), and personal liability (up to €500,000).
- **Deposit Protection** — Funds protected up to €100,000 by the German Deposit Guarantee Scheme.
- **100% Mobile** — Full account management via the N26 app or web app; account opening in minutes with identity verification.
- **Round-ups & Rules** — Automated saving tools to set money aside.
- **Real-time Notifications** — Instant spending alerts for every transaction.

explainability.content: N26 is a German fintech and mobile banking company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Berlin.

The free N26 Standard plan has no maintenance fees or minimum balance, provides a virtual Debit Mastercard usable for Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Wallet and Garmin Pay, and includes SEPA Instant Credit transfers.

N26 Smart costs €4.90 per month, adds a physical Mastercard debit card (choice of five colours), up to six virtual cards, three free domestic ATM withdrawals per month, and allows up to 10 Spaces sub‑accounts each with its own IBAN.
The Smart plan also includes a flexible Instant Savings account for easy saving and access to funds.

N26 Go costs €9.90 per month, includes all Smart features plus travel insurance from Allianz Assistance (covering travel delays, baggage loss, and medical emergencies abroad), fee‑free foreign‑currency ATM withdrawals worldwide, and three free stock/ETF trades per month.

N26 Metal costs €16.90 per month, bundles all Go benefits, upgrades the Mastercard to a stainless‑steel metal card, adds smartphone theft/damage cover up to €2,000, purchase protection, priority customer support, one free airport lounge pass per year, a market‑leading Instant Savings interest rate, and ten free stock/ETF trades per month.
Trading stocks, ETFs and ETCs through the N26 app costs €0.90 per transaction; Go customers receive three free trades per month and Metal customers receive ten free trades per month.
All N26 accounts are protected up to €100,000 by the German Deposit Guarantee Scheme.

N26 also offers business accounts: Business Standard (free), Business Smart (paid), Business Go (includes travel insurance and 0.1 % cashback on Mastercard purchases), and Business Metal (premium tier).

{"content":"## N26 Crypto — Cryptocurrency Trading Features

**N26 SE** is a German fintech and banking company headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013. It offers a cryptocurrency trading product called **N26 Crypto**, which is fully integrated into the N26 mobile banking app.

### Key Features

- **Wide coin selection:** N26 Crypto offers access to **over 350 cryptocurrencies** to buy and sell — one of the largest selections available in a European banking app. The initial launch started with 180+ coins.
- **In-app integration:** Crypto trading is accessible from the **"Trading" section** within the app's **"Finances" tab**, sitting alongside the user's main bank account, savings, and investment portfolio.
- **Instant transactions:** Customers select a coin and the amount they wish to trade; the cash equivalent is deducted from their bank balance, and coins appear in the N26 Crypto portfolio instantly. Selling is equally seamless — funds are made available immediately in the main bank account when a position is closed.
- **Portfolio visualization:** Clear visual graphs and real-time trading logs allow customers to track their crypto portfolio's development over time, including purchase history and portfolio value at any given point.
- **Drag-and-drop functionality:** Available for both buying and selling transactions.
- **Transparent fee structure:**
  - **N26 Metal customers:** 1% transaction fee for Bitcoin, 2% for all other cryptocurrencies (discount applies to trading amounts up to €5,000/month).
  - **All other N26 customers:** 1.5% for Bitcoin, 2.5% for other cryptocurrencies.
  - Fees are displayed and confirmed before each transaction.

### Partnership & Custody

N26 Crypto is offered in **partnership with Bitpanda** (specifically Bitpanda Asset Management GmbH), which manages the execution of trades and custody of coins.

### Market Availability

- **Initial launch:** Austria (late 2022).
- **Expanded to:** Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, France, and Spain, with rollout continuing to additional European markets.

### Sign-Up

Customers who have completed N26's identity verification and eligibility checks can access N26 Crypto directly within the app. A quick eligibility check is required before the first transaction.

## N26 Crypto — Cryptocurrency Trading Features

**N26 SE** is a German fintech and banking company headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013. It offers a cryptocurrency trading product called **N26 Crypto**, which is fully integrated into the N26 mobile banking app.

### Key Features

- **Wide coin selection:** N26 Crypto offers access to **over 350 cryptocurrencies** to buy and sell — one of the largest selections available in a European banking app. The initial launch started with 180+ coins.
- **In-app integration:** Crypto trading is accessible from the **"Trading" section** within the app's **"Finances" tab**, sitting alongside the user's main bank account, savings, and investment portfolio.
- **Instant transactions:** Customers select a coin and the amount they wish to trade; the cash equivalent is deducted from their bank balance, and coins appear in the N26 Crypto portfolio instantly. Selling is equally seamless — funds are made available immediately in the main bank account when a position is closed.
- **Portfolio visualization:** Clear visual graphs and real-time trading logs allow customers to track their crypto portfolio's development over time, including purchase history and portfolio value at any given point.
- **Drag-and-drop functionality:** Available for both buying and selling transactions.
- **Transparent fee structure:**
  - **N26 Metal customers:** 1% transaction fee for Bitcoin, 2% for all other cryptocurrencies (discount applies to trading amounts up to €5,000/month).
  - **All other N26 customers:** 1.5% for Bitcoin, 2.5% for other cryptocurrencies.
  - Fees are displayed and confirmed before each transaction.

### Partnership & Custody

N26 Crypto is offered in **partnership with Bitpanda** (specifically Bitpanda Asset Management GmbH), which manages the execution of trades and custody of coins.

### Market Availability

- **Initial launch:** Austria (late 2022).
- **Expanded to:** Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, France, and Spain, with rollout continuing to additional European markets.

### Sign-Up

Customers who have completed N26's identity verification and eligibility checks can access N26 Crypto directly within the app. A quick eligibility check is required before the first transaction.

N26, a German fintech and mobile banking company founded in 2013, offers a comprehensive range of products and account features across both personal and business banking segments:

## Personal Account Tiers

**N26 Standard (Free)**
- Virtual Debit Mastercard with no maintenance fees or minimum balance
- Mobile payments via Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Wallet, and Garmin Pay
- Insights spending tracker
- SEPA Instant Credit transfers

**N26 Smart (€4.90/month)**
- Physical Mastercard debit card (choice of 5 colors)
- Up to 6 virtual cards
- 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals per month
- Up to 10 Spaces sub-accounts with IBANs
- Shared Spaces feature
- Instant Savings account
- Rules for automatic saving

**N26 Go (€9.90/month)**
- All Smart features plus:
- Travel insurance by Allianz Assistance (travel/baggage delays, baggage loss, medical emergencies abroad up to €1,000,000/trip, trip cancellation up to €10,000)
- No foreign transaction fees
- Free foreign-currency ATM withdrawals worldwide
- 3 free stock/ETF trades per month

**N26 Metal (€16.90/month)**
- All Go features plus:
- Stainless-steel metal Mastercard (charcoal black, rose quartz, or slate grey)
- Extended insurance (smartphone theft/damage cover up to €2,000, purchase protection)
- 10 free stock/ETF trades per month
- Priority customer support
- One free airport lounge pass per year
- Market-leading Instant Savings interest rate
- Discounted crypto trading fees

## Business Accounts

N26 offers four business account tiers for freelancers and the self-employed:
- **Business Standard** (Free)
- **Business Smart** (Paid tier with enhanced features)
- **Business Go** (includes travel insurance by Allianz and 0.1% cashback on all Mastercard purchases)
- **Business Metal** (Premium business account)

## Key Product Features

**Spaces Sub-Accounts**
Launched in August 2018, Spaces allows customers to create up to 10 sub-accounts alongside their main account for budgeting and saving goals, each with its own IBAN (introduced in March 2022).

**Investment Products**
- **Stocks, ETFs & ETCs Trading**: Launched in January 2024, customers can buy and sell stocks, ETFs, and ETCs directly in the N26 app at €0.90 per trade (with free trades included on Go and Metal plans)

**N26 Crypto**
Launched initially in Austria in late 2022 and expanded to Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, France, and Spain:
- Access to over 350 cryptocurrencies (one of the largest selections in a European banking app)
- Fully integrated into the N26 app's "Trading" section
- Instant transactions with transparent fee structure
- N26 Metal customers: 1% fee for Bitcoin, 2% for other cryptocurrencies
- Other customers: 1.5% fee for Bitcoin, 2.5% for other cryptocurrencies
- Partnership with Bitpanda Asset Management GmbH for execution and custody

**Insurance Coverage**
Travel and personal insurance packages by Allianz Assistance on Go and Metal tiers, covering:
- Travel delays (up to €500)
- Trip cancellation/interruption (up to €10,000)
- Baggage loss (up to €2,000)
- Medical emergencies abroad (up to €1,000,000)
- Personal liability (up to €500,000)

**Additional Features**
- Instant Savings: Flexible savings account accessible anytime
- Rules & Round-ups: Automated saving tools
- Income Sorter: Automatic income distribution feature
- Real-time notifications for every transaction
- 100% mobile account management
- Deposit protection up to €100,000 by the German Deposit Guarantee Scheme

| **Ultra** | £55/mo | €65/mo | Unlimited airport lounge access, global data, partner subscriptions, cancellation cover |

#### **Key Personal Fees by Tier:**

**Currency Exchange:**
- **Standard:** Free up to £1,000/month; 1% fee beyond limit; 1% weekend surcharge
- **Plus:** Free up to £3,000/month; 0.5% fee beyond limit; 0.5% weekend surcharge
- **Premium/Metal/Ultra:** Unlimited free exchange; no weekend fees

**ATM Withdrawals:**
- **Standard:** £200 or 5 withdrawals free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Plus:** £200 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Premium:** £400 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Metal:** £800 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Ultra:** £2,000 free/month; 2% fee beyond

**International Transfers:**
- **Standard/Plus:** Standard fees apply
- **Premium:** 20% discount on transfer fees
- **Metal:** 40% discount on transfer fees
- **Ultra:** Unlimited transfers at no cost

- **Standard/Plus:** 1.49% per trade
- **Premium:** 0.99% per trade
- **Metal/Ultra:** 0.49% starting rate (reduces with volume)

**Stock Trading:**
- **Standard–Metal:** 0.25% commission (minimum £1)
- **Ultra:** 0.12% commission (minimum £1)

- **Standard/Plus:** £4.99
- **Premium/Metal/Ultra:** Free (first card)

Revolut Business offers four tiers with regional pricing:

| Plan | UK | Eurozone | US | Best For |
|------|-------|----------|-----|----------|
| **Basic** | £10/mo | €10/mo | $10/mo | Getting started with core features |
| **Grow** | From £30/mo | €30–35/mo | $40/mo | Managing spend with ease (save up to 14% annually) |
| **Scale** | From £90/mo | €90–135/mo | $140/mo | Expanding globally (save up to 28% annually) |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom | Custom | Tailored to exact business needs |

#### **Key Business Fees by Tier:**

**Local Transfers:**
- **Basic:** 10 free/month, then £0.20/€0.20 each
- **Grow:** 100 free/month, then £0.20/€0.20 each
- **Scale:** 1,000 free/month, then £0.20/€0.20 each
- **Enterprise:** Custom

**International Transfers:**
- **Basic:** 0 free (£5/€5 per transfer)
- **Grow:** 5 free/month, then £5/€5 each
- **Scale:** 25 free/month, then £5/€5 each
- **Enterprise:** Custom

**FX Exchange at Interbank Rate:**
- **Basic:** £1,000/€1,000 allowance
- **Grow:** Up to £15,000/€15,000
- **Scale:** Up to £60,000/€60,000
- **Enterprise:** Custom (markup applies beyond allowance)

**ATM Withdrawals:**
- All plans: 2% fee
- Daily limits: £3,000 (Basic) to £10,000 (Scale/Enterprise)

**Payment Acceptance (UK):**
- Domestic consumer cards: 1% + £0.20
- International/commercial cards: 2.8% + £0.20
- Revolut Pay (personal): 1% + £0.20
- Tap to Pay on iPhone: 1% + £0.20 (capped at £5)
- Chargebacks: £15 (refunded if won)

**Savings Interest (variable):**
- **Basic:** ~1% p.a.
- **Grow:** ~1.25% p.a.
- **Scale:** ~1.55% p.a.
- **Enterprise:** Up to ~2% p.a.

**Crypto Trading:**
- **Basic:** 1.49%
- **Grow:** 0.99%
- **Scale/Enterprise:** 0.49%

**Hardware:**
- Revolut Terminal: £169 + VAT
- Lite Terminal: £129 + VAT
- No monthly terminal fees

---

### **Recent Price Changes**

In 2026, Revolut notified UK customers of price increases for Plus, Premium, and Metal plans. As part of this change, Premium and Metal plans now include access to lifestyle app subscriptions (Tinder, Deliveroo, Financial Times, etc.), adding up to £1,730 in annual value depending on the plan tier.

---

### **Key Differences Across Tiers**

The main differentiators are:
1. **Monthly allowances** (FX exchange, ATM withdrawals, free transfers) increase significantly with higher tiers
2. **Fee percentages** decrease for premium tiers (especially for crypto, stock trading, and international transfers)
3. **Premium perks** like travel insurance, lounge access, and subscription bundles are exclusive to higher personal tiers
4. **Business plans** scale with transaction volume needs and offer better rates for high-volume operations

Annual subscriptions are available for Business Grow, Scale, and Enterprise plans, offering savings of up to 28%.

{"content":"# Revolut Pricing Plans, Tiers & Fees

Revolut offers two main product lines — **Personal** and **Business** — each with multiple tiers. Pricing varies by country; the figures below reflect UK (GBP) and Eurozone (EUR) pricing as of 2026.

---

## Personal Plans

| Plan | Monthly Fee (UK) | Monthly Fee (EUR) | Key Highlights |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | Free | Free | Basic money management, budgeting, send money abroad |
| **Plus** | £3.99/mo (or £40/yr) | €2.99/mo | Better spending-abroad limits, purchase insurance |
| **Premium** | £7.99/mo (or £80/yr) | €8.99/mo | Exclusive subscriptions, better savings rates, unlimited FX exchange |
| **Metal** | £14.99/mo (or £140/yr) | €15.99/mo | Travel insurance, enhanced limits, subscriptions worth ~£2,200/€2,700 annually |
| **Ultra** | £55/mo | €65/mo | Unlimited airport lounge access, global data, partner subscriptions, cancellation cover |

### Key Personal Fees

- **Currency exchange (weekdays):** Free up to a monthly limit (Standard: £1,000; Plus: £3,000; Premium/Metal/Ultra: unlimited). Beyond the limit, a fair-usage fee of 1% (Standard) or 0.5% (Plus) applies.
- **Weekend FX surcharge:** Standard 1%, Plus 0.5%, Premium/Metal/Ultra: no fee.
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to a monthly limit — Standard: £200 or 5 withdrawals; Plus: £200; Premium: £400; Metal: £800; Ultra: £2,000. Beyond the limit, a 2% fee applies.
- **International transfers:** Discounts by plan — Premium: 20% off fees; Metal: 40% off; Ultra: unlimited at no cost.
- **Crypto trading:** Tiered by plan and 30-day volume. Standard: 1.49%; Plus: 1.49%; Premium: 0.99%; Metal/Ultra: 0.49% (starting rate). Volume-based tiers reduce fees further (e.g. Ultra at ≥£250k volume: 0.29%).
- **Stock trading:** Commission-free trades included monthly (varies by plan); additional trades at 0.25% (Standard–Metal) or 0.12% (Ultra), minimum £1.
- **Card delivery:** Physical card costs £4.99 for Standard/Plus; free for Premium, Metal, and Ultra (first card).

---

## Business Plans

### UK Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic** | £10/mo | Getting started with core features |
| **Grow** | From £30/mo (save up to 14% annually) | Managing spend with ease |
| **Scale** | From £90/mo (save up to 28% annually) | Expanding globally with higher allowances |
| **Enterprise** | Custom pricing | Tailored to exact business needs |

### Eurozone Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | From €10/mo |
| **Grow** | From €30–€35/mo |
| **Scale** | From €90–€135/mo |
| **Enterprise** | Custom |

### US Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | From $10/mo |
| **Grow** | From $40/mo |
| **Scale** | From $140/mo |
| **Enterprise** | Custom |

### Key Business Fees

- **Local transfers:** Basic: 10 free/mo, then £0.20/€0.20 each; Grow: 100 free/mo; Scale: 1,000 free/mo; Enterprise: custom.
- **International transfers:** Basic: 0 free (£5/€5 per transfer); Grow: 5 free/mo then £5/€5; Scale: 25 free/mo then £5/€5; Enterprise: custom.
- **Revolut-to-Revolut transfers:** Free on all plans.
- **FX exchange at interbank rate:** Basic: £1,000/€1,000; Grow: up to £15,000/€15,000; Scale: up to £60,000/€60,000; Enterprise: custom. Beyond the allowance, a markup applies.
- **ATM withdrawals:** 2% fee on all plans; daily limits range from £3,000 (Basic) to £10,000 (Scale/Enterprise).
- **Payment acceptance (UK):** Domestic consumer cards: 1% + £0.20; International/commercial cards: 2.8% + £0.20; Revolut Pay (personal): 1% + £0.20; Tap to Pay on iPhone: 1% + £0.20 (capped at £5). Chargebacks: £15 (refunded if dispute won).
- **Savings interest (variable):** Basic: ~1% p.a.; Grow: ~1.25% p.a.; Scale: ~1.55% p.a.; Enterprise: up to ~2% p.a.
- **Flexible Cash Funds APY (as of June 2026):** Varies by plan — e.g. USD: 2.15%–3.49% APY; GBP: 2.43%–3.43% APY; EUR: 1.24%–1.94% APY.
- **Crypto (Business):** 1.49% (Basic), 0.99% (Grow), 0.49% (Scale/Enterprise).
- **Hardware:** Revolut Terminal: £169 + VAT; Lite Terminal: £129 + VAT. No monthly terminal fees.

Annual subscriptions are available for Grow, Scale, and Enterprise plans, offering savings of up to 28%.

---

# Revolut Pricing Plans, Tiers & Fees

Revolut offers two main product lines — **Personal** and **Business** — each with multiple tiers. Pricing varies by country; the figures below reflect UK (GBP) and Eurozone (EUR) pricing as of 2026.

---

## Personal Plans

| Plan | Monthly Fee (UK) | Monthly Fee (EUR) | Key Highlights |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | Free | Free | Basic money management, budgeting, send money abroad |
| **Plus** | £3.99/mo (or £40/yr) | €2.99/mo | Better spending-abroad limits, purchase insurance |
| **Premium** | £7.99/mo (or £80/yr) | €8.99/mo | Exclusive subscriptions, better savings rates, unlimited FX exchange |
| **Metal** | £14.99/mo (or £140/yr) | €15.99/mo | Travel insurance, enhanced limits, subscriptions worth ~£2,200/€2,700 annually |
| **Ultra** | £55/mo | €65/mo | Unlimited airport lounge access, global data, partner subscriptions, cancellation cover |

### Key Personal Fees

- **Currency exchange (weekdays):** Free up to a monthly limit (Standard: £1,000; Plus: £3,000; Premium/Metal/Ultra: unlimited). Beyond the limit, a fair-usage fee of 1% (Standard) or 0.5% (Plus) applies.
- **Weekend FX surcharge:** Standard 1%, Plus 0.5%, Premium/Metal/Ultra: no fee.
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to a monthly limit — Standard: £200 or 5 withdrawals; Plus: £200; Premium: £400; Metal: £800; Ultra: £2,000. Beyond the limit, a 2% fee applies.
- **International transfers:** Discounts by plan — Premium: 20% off fees; Metal: 40% off; Ultra: unlimited at no cost.
- **Crypto trading:** Tiered by plan and 30-day volume. Standard: 1.49%; Plus: 1.49%; Premium: 0.99%; Metal/Ultra: 0.49% (starting rate). Volume-based tiers reduce fees further (e.g. Ultra at ≥£250k volume: 0.29%).
- **Stock trading:** Commission-free trades included monthly (varies by plan); additional trades at 0.25% (Standard–Metal) or 0.12% (Ultra), minimum £1.
- **Card delivery:** Physical card costs £4.99 for Standard/Plus; free for Premium, Metal, and Ultra (first card).

---

## Business Plans

### UK Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic** | £10/mo | Getting started with core features |
| **Grow** | From £30/mo (save up to 14% annually) | Managing spend with ease |
| **Scale** | From £90/mo (save up to 28% annually) | Expanding globally with higher allowances |
| **Enterprise** | Custom pricing | Tailored to exact business needs |

### Eurozone Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | From €10/mo |
| **Grow** | From €30–€35/mo |
| **Scale** | From €90–€135/mo |
| **Enterprise** | Custom |

### US Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Fee |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | From $10/mo |
| **Grow** | From $40/mo |
| **Scale** | From $140/mo |
| **Enterprise** | Custom |

### Key Business Fees

- **Local transfers:** Basic: 10 free/mo, then £0.20/€0.20 each; Grow: 100 free/mo; Scale: 1,000 free/mo; Enterprise: custom.
- **International transfers:** Basic: 0 free (£5/€5 per transfer); Grow: 5 free/mo then £5/€5; Scale: 25 free/mo then £5/€5; Enterprise: custom.
- **Revolut-to-Revolut transfers:** Free on all plans.
- **FX exchange at interbank rate:** Basic: £1,000/€1,000; Grow: up to £15,000/€15,000; Scale: up to £60,000/€60,000; Enterprise: custom. Beyond the allowance, a markup applies.
- **ATM withdrawals:** 2% fee on all plans; daily limits range from £3,000 (Basic) to £10,000 (Scale/Enterprise).
- **Payment acceptance (UK):** Domestic consumer cards: 1% + £0.20; International/commercial cards: 2.8% + £0.20; Revolut Pay (personal): 1% + £0.20; Tap to Pay on iPhone: 1% + £0.20 (capped at £5). Chargebacks: £15 (refunded if dispute won).
- **Savings interest (variable):** Basic: ~1% p.a.; Grow: ~1.25% p.a.; Scale: ~1.55% p.a.; Enterprise: up to ~2% p.a.

## Revolut's Pricing Plans, Tiers, and Fee Structure

Revolut offers two main product lines—**Personal** and **Business**—each with multiple tiers that differ significantly in pricing and features.

---

### **Personal Plans**

Revolut's personal banking has five tiers:

| Plan | UK Monthly Fee | EUR Monthly Fee | Key Features |
|------|----------------|-----------------|--------------|
| **Standard** | Free | Free | Basic money management, budgeting, send money abroad |
| **Plus** | £3.99/mo (£40/yr) | €2.99/mo | Better spending-abroad limits, purchase insurance |
| **Premium** | £7.99/mo (£80/yr) | €8.99/mo | Exclusive subscriptions, better savings rates, unlimited FX exchange |
| **Metal** | £14.99/mo (£140/yr) | €15.99/mo | Travel insurance, enhanced limits, subscriptions worth ~£2,200/€2,700 annually |
| **Ultra** | £55/mo | €65/mo | Unlimited airport lounge access, global data, partner subscriptions, cancellation cover |

#### **Key Personal Fees by Tier:**

**Currency Exchange:**
- **Standard:** Free up to £1,000/month; 1% fee beyond limit; 1% weekend surcharge
- **Plus:** Free up to £3,000/month; 0.5% fee beyond limit; 0.5% weekend surcharge
- **Premium/Metal/Ultra:** Unlimited free exchange; no weekend fees

**ATM Withdrawals:**
- **Standard:** £200 or 5 withdrawals free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Plus:** £200 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Premium:** £400 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Metal:** £800 free/month; 2% fee beyond
- **Ultra:** £2,000 free/month; 2% fee beyond

**International Transfers:**
- **Standard/Plus:** Standard fees apply
- **Premium:** 20% discount on transfer fees
- **Metal:** 40% discount on transfer fees
- **Ultra:** Unlimited transfers at no cost

**Crypto Trading:**
- **Standard/Plus:** 1.49% per trade
- **Premium:** 0.99% per trade
- **Metal/Ultra:** 0.49% starting rate (reduces with volume)

**Stock Trading:**
- **Standard–Metal:** 0.25% commission (minimum £1)
- **Ultra:** 0.12% commission (minimum £1)

**Physical Card:**
- **Standard/Plus:** £4.99
- **Premium/Metal/Ultra:** Free (first card)

---

### **Business Plans**

Revolut Business offers four tiers with regional pricing:

| Plan | UK | Eurozone | US | Best For |
|------|-------|----------|-----|----------|
| **Basic** | £10/mo | €10/mo | $10/mo | Getting started with core features |
| **Grow** | From £30/mo | €30–35/mo | $40/mo | Managing spend with ease (save up to 14% annually) |
| **Scale** | From £90/mo | €90–135/mo | $140/mo | Expanding globally (save up to 28% annually) |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom | Custom | Tailored to exact business needs |

#### **Key Business Fees by Tier:**

**Local Transfers:**
- **Basic:** 10 free/month, then £0.20/€0.20 each
- **Grow:** 100 free/month, then £0.20/€0.20 each

What do users value and complain about in the competitor's (Revolut) app reviews?
answer:
## What Users Value About Revolut's App

**Speed and Ease of Use**
Users consistently praise Revolut's intuitive interface and fast transaction processing. The app is described as simple and full of features, making financial management straightforward.

**International Capabilities**
Multi-currency accounts, competitive exchange rates, and the ability to send money to 160+ countries are among the most-cited advantages. Travelers and expats particularly value spending abroad with low fees, with users able to hold up to 36 currencies in-app and spend in 150+ currencies.

**All-in-One "Super App"**
Revolut combines banking, payments, investing (stocks and crypto), expense tracking, and budgeting tools in a single platform, which users find highly convenient. This comprehensive approach eliminates the need for multiple financial apps.

**Lower Fees Than Traditional Banks**
Users highlight significant savings on foreign exchange, transfers, and everyday spending compared to legacy banks.

**Security Features**
Two-factor authentication, disposable virtual cards, single-use virtual cards for extra protection, and real-time transaction alerts are appreciated by users. The 24/7 financial crime team and AI-based fraud detection algorithms provide peace of mind.

**Continuous Improvement**
Long-term users note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time, demonstrating ongoing innovation.

**Overall Ratings**
The app maintains strong ratings of 4.7/5 on the App Store and 4.9/5 on Revolut's own review pages (as of August-September 2026), with hundreds of thousands of reviews showing generally positive sentiment.

---

## What Users Complain About

**1. Customer Support (Most Frequent Complaint)**
Users report slow, unhelpful responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent—especially when locked out of their accounts. This is the most consistent pain point across reviews.

**2. Account Restrictions and Frozen Funds**
Multiple users report accounts being restricted or funds frozen without clear explanation or timely resolution. This causes significant frustration and anxiety, particularly when users need access to their money urgently.

**3. Hidden or Unexpected Fees**
Charges for crypto transactions, subscription cancellations, and certain currency exchanges catch users off guard. Users feel these fees are not clearly communicated upfront.

**4. Fraud and Scam Complaint Handling**
Revolut recorded the highest number of fraud complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS):
- **2024:** 3,242 APP (Authorised Push Payment) fraud complaints and 2,631 other fraud/scam complaints
- **2025 (first 8 months):** 1,333 APP fraud complaints with a 37% uphold rate (meaning the FOS sided with the customer in 37% of cases)
- Which? flagged Revolut as the worst UK firm for fraud complaints as of October 2025

**5. Data Privacy Concerns**
Some users express unease about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps and recent policy changes around data collection.

**6. Difficulty Deleting Accounts**
Users report cumbersome processes when trying to close their accounts or access support while locked out.

---

## Summary

Users primarily value Revolut for its **speed, low-cost international transfers, multi-currency support, and feature-rich all-in-one platform**. The main areas of dissatisfaction center on **customer support quality, unexplained account freezes, hidden fees, and fraud complaint handling**. While the app maintains high ratings, the volume of fraud-related complaints escalated to regulators represents a notable concern that distinguishes Revolut from competitors.

## Revolut App: User Reviews, Complaints & What Users Value

### Overall Sentiment

Revolut enjoys strong overall ratings — **4.7/5 on the App Store** and **4.9/5 on its own review pages** (as of August–September 2026), with hundreds of thousands of reviews. The general sentiment across recent reviews (last 90 days) is **positive**, though several recurring pain points persist.

---

### What Users Value Most (Pros)

- **Speed and ease of use** — Users consistently praise the app's intuitive interface and fast transaction processing.
- **International capabilities** — Multi-currency accounts, competitive exchange rates, and the ability to send money to 160+ countries are among the most-cited advantages. Travellers and expats particularly value spending abroad with low fees.
- **All-in-one "super app"** — Revolut combines banking, payments, investing (stocks and crypto), expense tracking, and budgeting tools in a single platform, which users find convenient.
- **Lower fees than traditional banks** — Users highlight savings on foreign exchange, transfers, and everyday spending compared to legacy banks.
- **Security features** — Two-factor authentication, disposable virtual cards, and real-time transaction alerts are appreciated.
- **Continuous improvement** — Long-term users note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time.

> *"I've been using Revolut for the past 5 years and it's my main account, even though I have 4+ accounts. It's simple, full of features, and easy to use."* — Michael, UK

---

### Top User Complaints (Cons)

1. **Customer support** — The most frequent complaint. Users report slow, unhelpful responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent — especially when locked out of their account.

2. **Account restrictions and frozen funds** — Multiple users report accounts being restricted or funds frozen without clear explanation or timely resolution. This is a major source of frustration and anxiety.

3. **Hidden or unexpected fees** — Charges for crypto transactions, subscription cancellations, and certain currency exchanges catch users off guard.

4. **Fraud and scam complaint handling** — Revolut recorded the **highest number of fraud complaints** escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS) in both 2024 and 2025:
   - **2024:** 3,242 APP (Authorised Push Payment) fraud complaints and 2,631 other fraud/scam complaints referred to the FOS.
   - **2025 (first 8 months):** 1,333 APP fraud complaints referred to the FOS, with a 37% uphold rate (i.e., the FOS sided with the customer in 37% of cases).
   - Which? flagged Revolut as the **worst UK firm for fraud complaints** as of October 2025.

5. **Data privacy concerns** — Some users express unease about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps and recent policy changes around data collection.

6. **Difficulty deleting accounts** — Users report cumbersome processes when trying to close their accounts or access support while locked out.

---

### Recent Developments (2026)

- Revolut now serves **80 million customers worldwide**.
- The company received **conditional approval for a US national bank charter** from the OCC in September 2026, with plans to launch as a federally regulated bank in the US by 2027.
- Revolut also secured banking licences in **France** and **Australia** in 2026, and was authorised to operate a bank in the **UK** in March 2026.
- An **€11 million fine** was imposed by the Italian competition authority in April 2026 over "unfair commercial practices."

---

### Summary

Users value Revolut primarily for its **speed, low-cost international transfers, multi-currency support, and feature-rich app**. The main areas of dissatisfaction centre on **customer support quality, unexplained account freezes, hidden fees, and fraud complaint handling**. While the app's ratings remain high, the volume of fraud-related complaints escalated to regulators is a notable concern.

input.answer:
## What Users Value About Revolut's App

**Speed and Ease of Use**
Users consistently praise Revolut's intuitive interface and fast transaction processing. The app is described as simple and full of features, making financial management straightforward.

**International Capabilities**
Multi-currency accounts, competitive exchange rates, and the ability to send money to 160+ countries are among the most-cited advantages. Travelers and expats particularly value spending abroad with low fees, with users able to hold up to 36 currencies in-app and spend in 150+ currencies.

**All-in-One "Super App"**
Revolut combines banking, payments, investing (stocks and crypto), expense tracking, and budgeting tools in a single platform, which users find highly convenient. This comprehensive approach eliminates the need for multiple financial apps.

**Lower Fees Than Traditional Banks**
Users highlight significant savings on foreign exchange, transfers, and everyday spending compared to legacy banks.

**Security Features**
Two-factor authentication, disposable virtual cards, single-use virtual cards for extra protection, and real-time transaction alerts are appreciated by users. The 24/7 financial crime team and AI-based fraud detection algorithms provide peace of mind.

**Continuous Improvement**
Long-term users note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time, demonstrating ongoing innovation.

**Overall Ratings**
The app maintains strong ratings of 4.7/5 on the App Store and 4.9/5 on Revolut's own review pages (as of August-September 2026), with hundreds of thousands of reviews showing generally positive sentiment.

---

## What Users Complain About

**1. Customer Support (Most Frequent Complaint)**
Users report slow, unhelpful responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent—especially when locked out of their accounts. This is the most consistent pain point across reviews.

**2. Account Restrictions and Frozen Funds**
Multiple users report accounts being restricted or funds frozen without clear explanation or timely resolution. This causes significant frustration and anxiety, particularly when users need access to their money urgently.

**3. Hidden or Unexpected Fees**
Charges for crypto transactions, subscription cancellations, and certain currency exchanges catch users off guard. Users feel these fees are not clearly communicated upfront.

**4. Fraud and Scam Complaint Handling**
Revolut recorded the highest number of fraud complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS):
- **2024:** 3,242 APP (Authorised Push Payment) fraud complaints and 2,631 other fraud/scam complaints
- **2025 (first 8 months):** 1,333 APP fraud complaints with a 37% uphold rate (meaning the FOS sided with the customer in 37% of cases)
- Which? flagged Revolut as the worst UK firm for fraud complaints as of October 2025

**5. Data Privacy Concerns**
Some users express unease about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps and recent policy changes around data collection.

**6. Difficulty Deleting Accounts**
Users report cumbersome processes when trying to close their accounts or access support while locked out.

---

## Summary

Users primarily value Revolut for its **speed, low-cost international transfers, multi-currency support, and feature-rich all-in-one platform**. The main areas of dissatisfaction center on **customer support quality, unexplained account freezes, hidden fees, and fraud complaint handling**. While the app maintains high ratings, the volume of fraud-related complaints escalated to regulators represents a notable concern that distinguishes Revolut from competitors.

## BNP Paribas Leadership Organizational Structure

BNP Paribas has a hierarchical leadership structure consisting of **General Management** and an **Executive Committee** that meets at least once a week.

### General Management (6 Members)

The General Management comprises a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), two Chief Operating Officers (COOs), and three Deputy Chief Operating Officers (Deputy COOs):

**1. Jean-Laurent Bonnafé - Director and Chief Executive Officer**
- Bears overall responsibility for the management of the entire Group
- All operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility
- Invested with extensive powers for Group management

**2. Yann Gérardin - Chief Operating Officer**
- Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (since September 1, 2025)
- Oversees capital markets, securities services, investment banking, financing, and advisory

**3. Thierry Laborde - Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)
- Oversees retail banking across domestic markets, international retail, personal finance, and specialized services

**4. Renaud Dumora - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Investment & Protection Services (IPS)
- Oversees insurance, asset management, wealth management, and real estate

**5. Yannick Jung - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Commercial & Personal Banking businesses in the euro zone within CPBS
- Focuses on retail banking operations in eurozone markets

**6. Olivier Osty - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (since September 1, 2025)
- Manages CIB's operational execution

### Executive Committee - Additional 14 Members

**Business Line Heads:**

**7. Michael Anseeuw**
- Director, CEO and Chairman of the Executive Board of BNP Paribas Fortis
- Responsible for Belgium domestic market operations

**8. Elena Goitini**
- CEO of BNL
- Responsible for Italy domestic market operations

**9. Isabelle Loc**
- Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France
- Manages French retail banking operations

**10. Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux**
- CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif
- Leads the Group's insurance arm

**11. Sandro Pierri**
- CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management
- Joined the Executive Committee on March 30, 2026
- Reports to Renaud Dumora

**12. Gilles Zeitoun**
- Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance
- Joined the Executive Committee on January 1, 2026
- Oversees consumer credit business in Europe

**Central Function Heads:**

**13. Lars Machenil - Chief Financial Officer**
- In position since 2012
- Responsible for all financial management and reporting

**14. Frank Roncey - Chief Risk Officer**
- In position since 2014
- Oversees Group-wide risk management

**15. Stéphanie Maarek - Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance)**
- Ensures regulatory compliance across the Group

**16. Philippe Maillard - Chief Operating Officer (Group COO)**
- Oversees operational functions including IT, procurement, and internal consulting

**17. Marc Camus - Chief Information Officer**
- Appointed April 2025
- Leads the Group's IT strategy, system security, operational efficiency, and customer experience through AI and cloud computing
- Reports to Philippe Maillard (COO)

**18. Sarah Roussel - Group Head of Human Resources**
- Appointed 2026, succeeding Sofia Merlo
- Reports to Philippe Maillard

**19. Élise Hermant - Head of Communications**
- Oversees the Group's communication and reputation initiatives

**20. Anne Pointet - Head of Company Engagement**
- Responsible for the Group's positioning on environmental and social inclusion matters, CSR, and philanthropy

### Three Main Business Divisions

The organizational structure operates through three main divisions:

1. **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** - Led by Yann Gérardin (Executive Chairman) and Olivier Osty (CEO)
2. **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** - Led by Renaud Dumora
3. **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** - Led by Thierry Laborde and Yannick Jung

{"content":"## BNP Paribas Executive Committee — Members and Responsibilities

The Executive Committee of BNP Paribas brings together the **General Management** (CEO + two Chief Operating Officers + three Deputy Chief Operating Officers) and **14 additional members** — heads of business lines and central functions. The committee meets at least once a week.

---

### General Management

| Member | Role |
|---|---|
| **Jean-Laurent Bonnafé** | Director and **Chief Executive Officer**. Bears overall responsibility for the management of the Group; all operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility. |
| **Yann Gérardin** | **Chief Operating Officer** of BNP Paribas and **Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** (since 1 September 2025). |
| **Thierry Laborde** | **Chief Operating Officer** of BNP Paribas, in charge of **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)**. |
| **Renaud Dumora** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer**, in charge of **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)**. |
| **Yannick Jung** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer**, in charge of the **Commercial & Personal Banking businesses in the euro zone** within CPBS. |
| **Olivier Osty** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer** and **Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** (since 1 September 2025). |

---

### Other Executive Committee Members

| Member | Role |
|---|---|
| **Michael Anseeuw** | Director, **CEO and Chairman of the Executive Board of BNP Paribas Fortis** (Belgium domestic market). |
| **Marc Camus** | **Chief Information Officer** (since April 2025). Leads the Group's IT strategy — system security, operational efficiency, and customer experience through technologies such as AI and cloud computing. Reports to the COO. |
| **Elena Goitini** | **CEO of BNL** (Italy domestic market). |
| **Élise Hermant** | **Head of Communications**. Oversees the Group's communication and reputation initiatives. |
| **Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux** | **CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif** (insurance arm). |
| **Isabelle Loc** | **Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France**. |
| **Stéphanie Maarek** | **Head of Compliance** (Chief Compliance Officer). |
| **Lars Machenil** | **Chief Financial Officer** (since 2012). |
| **Philippe Maillard** | **Chief Operating Officer** (Group COO). Oversees operational functions including IT, procurement, and internal consulting. |
| **Sandro Pierri** | **CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management** (joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026). Reports to Renaud Dumora. |
| **Anne Pointet** | **Head of Company Engagement**. Responsible for the Group's positioning on environmental and social inclusion matters, CSR, and philanthropy. |
| **Frank Roncey** | **Chief Risk Officer** (since 2014). |
| **Sarah Roussel** | **Group Head of Human Resources** (appointed 2026, succeeding Sofia Merlo). Reports to Philippe Maillard. |
| **Gilles Zeitoun** | **Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance** (joined the Executive Committee as of 1 January 2026, succeeding Charlotte Dennery). |

---

### Group Structure

BNP Paribas operates through **three main divisions**:

- **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** — capital markets, securities services, investment banking, financing, and advisory (overseen by Gérardin/Osty).
- **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** — insurance, asset management, wealth management, and real estate (overseen by Dumora).

## BNP Paribas Executive Committee — Members and Responsibilities

The Executive Committee of BNP Paribas brings together the **General Management** (CEO + two Chief Operating Officers + three Deputy Chief Operating Officers) and **14 additional members** — heads of business lines and central functions. The committee meets at least once a week.

---

### General Management

| Member | Role |
|---|---|
| **Jean-Laurent Bonnafé** | Director and **Chief Executive Officer**. Bears overall responsibility for the management of the Group; all operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility. |
| **Yann Gérardin** | **Chief Operating Officer** of BNP Paribas and **Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** (since 1 September 2025). |
| **Thierry Laborde** | **Chief Operating Officer** of BNP Paribas, in charge of **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)**. |
| **Renaud Dumora** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer**, in charge of **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)**. |
| **Yannick Jung** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer**, in charge of the **Commercial & Personal Banking businesses in the euro zone** within CPBS. |
| **Olivier Osty** | **Deputy Chief Operating Officer** and **Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** (since 1 September 2025). |

---

### Other Executive Committee Members

| Member | Role |
|---|---|
| **Michael Anseeuw** | Director, **CEO and Chairman of the Executive Board of BNP Paribas Fortis** (Belgium domestic market). |
| **Marc Camus** | **Chief Information Officer** (since April 2025). Leads the Group's IT strategy — system security, operational efficiency, and customer experience through technologies such as AI and cloud computing. Reports to the COO. |
| **Elena Goitini** | **CEO of BNL** (Italy domestic market). |
| **Élise Hermant** | **Head of Communications**. Oversees the Group's communication and reputation initiatives. |
| **Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux** | **CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif** (insurance arm). |
| **Isabelle Loc** | **Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France**. |
| **Stéphanie Maarek** | **Head of Compliance** (Chief Compliance Officer). |
| **Lars Machenil** | **Chief Financial Officer** (since 2012). |
| **Philippe Maillard** | **Chief Operating Officer** (Group COO). Oversees operational functions including IT, procurement, and internal consulting. |
| **Sandro Pierri** | **CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management** (joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026). Reports to Renaud Dumora. |
| **Anne Pointet** | **Head of Company Engagement**. Responsible for the Group's positioning on environmental and social inclusion matters, CSR, and philanthropy. |
| **Frank Roncey** | **Chief Risk Officer** (since 2014). |
| **Sarah Roussel** | **Group Head of Human Resources** (appointed 2026, succeeding Sofia Merlo). Reports to Philippe Maillard. |
| **Gilles Zeitoun** | **Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance** (joined the Executive Committee as of 1 January 2026, succeeding Charlotte Dennery). |

---

### Group Structure

BNP Paribas operates through **three main divisions**:

- **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** — capital markets, securities services, investment banking, financing, and advisory (overseen by Gérardin/Osty).
- **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** — insurance, asset management, wealth management, and real estate (overseen by Dumora).
- **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** — retail banking across domestic markets (France, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg), international retail, personal finance, and specialised services (overseen by Laborde/Jung).

## BNP Paribas Leadership Organizational Structure

BNP Paribas has a hierarchical leadership structure consisting of **General Management** and an **Executive Committee** that meets at least once a week.

### General Management (6 Members)

The General Management comprises a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), two Chief Operating Officers (COOs), and three Deputy Chief Operating Officers (Deputy COOs):

**1. Jean-Laurent Bonnafé - Director and Chief Executive Officer**
- Bears overall responsibility for the management of the entire Group
- All operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility
- Invested with extensive powers for Group management

**2. Yann Gérardin - Chief Operating Officer**
- Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (since September 1, 2025)
- Oversees capital markets, securities services, investment banking, financing, and advisory

**3. Thierry Laborde - Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)
- Oversees retail banking across domestic markets, international retail, personal finance, and specialized services

**4. Renaud Dumora - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Investment & Protection Services (IPS)
- Oversees insurance, asset management, wealth management, and real estate

**5. Yannick Jung - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- In charge of Commercial & Personal Banking businesses in the euro zone within CPBS
- Focuses on retail banking operations in eurozone markets

**6. Olivier Osty - Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (since September 1, 2025)
- Manages CIB's operational execution

### Executive Committee - Additional 14 Members

**Business Line Heads:**

**7. Michael Anseeuw**
- Director, CEO and Chairman of the Executive Board of BNP Paribas Fortis
- Responsible for Belgium domestic market operations

**8. Elena Goitini**
- CEO of BNL
- Responsible for Italy domestic market operations

**9. Isabelle Loc**
- Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France
- Manages French retail banking operations

**10. Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux**
- CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif
- Leads the Group's insurance arm

**11. Sandro Pierri**
- CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management
- Joined the Executive Committee on March 30, 2026
- Reports to Renaud Dumora

**12. Gilles Zeitoun**
- Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance
- Joined the Executive Committee on January 1, 2026
- Oversees consumer credit business in Europe

**Central Function Heads:**

**13. Lars Machenil - Chief Financial Officer**
- In position since 2012
- Responsible for all financial management and reporting

**14. Frank Roncey - Chief Risk Officer**
- In position since 2014
- Oversees Group-wide risk management

**15. Stéphanie Maarek - Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance)**
- Ensures regulatory compliance across the Group

**16. Philippe Maillard - Chief Operating Officer (Group COO)**
- Oversees operational functions including IT, procurement, and internal consulting

**17. Marc Camus - Chief Information Officer**
- Appointed April 2025
- Leads the Group's IT strategy, system security, operational efficiency, and customer experience through AI and cloud computing
- Reports to Philippe Maillard (COO)

**18. Sarah Roussel - Group Head of Human Resources**
- Appointed 2026, succeeding Sofia Merlo
- Reports to Philippe Maillard

**19. Élise Hermant - Head of Communications**
- Oversees the Group's communication and reputation initiatives

**20. Anne Pointet - Head of Company Engagement**
- Responsible for the Group's positioning on environmental and social inclusion matters, CSR, and philanthropy

### Three Main Business Divisions

The organizational structure operates through three main divisions:

1. **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** - Led by Yann Gérardin (Executive Chairman) and Olivier Osty (CEO)
2. **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** - Led by Renaud Dumora
3. **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** - Led by Thierry Laborde and Yannick Jung

query: What is the average CET1 capital ratio and NPL ratio of EU banks in the latest quarter?
answer:
Based on the latest available data from the European Banking Authority (EBA), the average financial ratios for EU banks are:

## CET1 Capital Ratio
**16.3%** as of Q4 2025 (the most recent quarter with complete data)

This represents the aggregate Common Equity Tier 1 ratio for EU domestic banking groups and stand-alone banks. The CET1 ratio has remained strong and stable, hovering around 16.2-16.4% throughout 2025.

## NPL Ratio
**1.8%** as of Q3 2025 (the most recent quarter with complete NPL data)

The non-performing loan ratio stood at 1.8% with NPL volumes broadly stable at approximately €373 billion. This represents a significant improvement from 6% in 2015 and continues a multi-year downward trend in asset quality issues.

### Additional Context
- The Q3 2025 data was published by the EBA in December 2025 through their Risk Dashboard
- Consumer credit and SME loans continue to show the highest NPL ratios within the sector
- Stage 2 loans (watch-list) decreased to 9.3%, and the cost of risk stood at 0.47%, the lowest since Q3 2023
- The sector's overall capital requirements and guidance for 2026 remain steady at approximately 11.2%
- EU/EEA banks reported a return on assets of 1.2% in Q1 2026

The data confirms that EU banks maintain strong capital buffers and stable asset quality despite heightened macroeconomic and geopolitical risks.

## EU Banks — CET1 Capital Ratio & NPL Ratio (Latest Available Data)

### CET1 Capital Ratio

The aggregate **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio** for EU banks has remained strong and on an upward trend:

| Quarter | CET1 Ratio |
|---------|-----------|
| Q4 2025 | **16.3%** |
| Q3 2025 | 16.43% |
| Q2 2025 | 16.41% |
| Q1 2025 | 16.21% |
| Q4 2024 | 16.36% |

The latest available aggregate figure is **16.3% as of Q4 2025**, based on EU domestic banking groups and stand-alone banks. For Q1 2026, the EBA reported the sector's average return on assets at 1.2%, and the CET1 ratio stood at **15.2%** for Greek banks specifically (up from 12.6% four years earlier), while overall EU/EEA CET1 requirements and guidance for 2026 remain steady at approximately **11.2%**.

### NPL Ratio

The **non-performing loan (NPL) ratio** for EU/EEA banks has continued its long-term decline:

- As of **Q3 2025** (the latest EBA Risk Dashboard published in December 2025), the aggregate NPL ratio stood at **1.8%**, with NPL volumes broadly stable at approximately **€373 billion**.
- This represents a dramatic improvement from 6% in 2015 and continues a multi-year downward trend. The NPL ratio has fallen to around **2%** on a sector-wide basis, as confirmed by ECB commentary from September 2026.
- Consumer credit and SME loans continue to show the highest NPL ratios within the sector.
- Stage 2 loans (watch-list) continued decreasing slowly to 9.3%, and the cost of risk stood at 0.47%, the lowest since Q3 2023.

### Context

- In Q2 2026 earnings, **83% of European banks beat pre-tax profit expectations**, and most upgraded full-year guidance due to higher revenues.
- The Stoxx 600 Banks Index is up around 21% year-to-date in 2026, reflecting continued investor confidence.
- Euro zone banks have been tightening credit standards amid geopolitical risks (Iran war, energy price pressures), which could affect future asset quality.
- The EU has delayed implementation of Basel III trading-risk capital rules by three years (2027–2029) to maintain a level playing field with the US and UK.

> **Note:** The latest publicly available EBA Risk Dashboard covers Q3 2025 data (published December 2025). The Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 dashboards may have been published or are forthcoming; the figures above represent the most recent confirmed aggregate data.
